statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. All 24 published hours fall inside the scheduled weekend closure of CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD, so no pathological Nasdaq-100 price path can form inside the window. Stress remains in the elevated band because a post-crisis long end, an elevated crude complex and a restricted Hormuz corridor are unresolved, not because any drawdown was observed.
recommendation: Tail stays far below the block threshold in every published hour: no tradable Nasdaq-100 venue exists before the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, thirteen hours beyond the final slot. Stress describes a 5.18% 10-year, $92.41 WTI and the reported refusal of Iran's seven-day Hormuz plan rather than any observed mean-reversion failure. Reopen gap risk falls outside this window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 remains inside the scheduled weekend closure after an orderly Friday advance to within 0.5% of its record; Tail holds at its halt floor while a 5.18% 10-year, $92 crude and the reported refusal of Iran's Hormuz plan keep Stress elevated
body: Every Nasdaq-100 venue has been shut since the Friday 21:00Z settle, and the whole 24-hour published window closes thirteen hours before CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday. Friday's session was orderly and two-sided. Cash NDX closed 30,608.14, up 129.28 points or 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.19% below the session high, against a 30,478.86 previous close and a 30,770.63 52-week high; the broader tape finished its first winning week in three with the S&P 500 up 0.51% to 7,743.41, the Nasdaq Composite up 0.48% to 27,068.72 and the Dow up 0.93% to 51,828.62. December NQ futures settled 30,889.25, +0.40%, in a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range, and VIX closed 14.87, -5.11%, inside 14.68-15.94. None of the inherited Tail amplifiers were present at the settle: retracements occurred repeatedly, no session extreme was held into the bell, and there was no repeated extension after a failed pullback. Tail therefore sits at 8, its halt floor, for the current hour and stays between 7 and 8 across the window, because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path and none can exist before the reopen. Stress at 47 reflects unresolved conditions rather than observed losses. The H.15 September 24 column puts the 10-year at 5.18%, the 2-year at 4.87% and the 30-year at 5.47%; Friday reporting tied the long-end move to the University of Michigan final September sentiment reading of 48.1, down from 51.7 in August, and described the market shrugging off the bond sell-off rather than resolving it. That 10-year level is the highest since the financial-crisis era. WTI eased 2.33% to $92.41 and Brent fell 2.14% to $104.32, capping a roughly 7.4% weekly decline on mixed signals over peace prospects and recovering regional energy flows. That optimism has since been undercut: multiple outlets reporting on September 26, citing a Wall Street Journal account of unnamed US officials, say the seven-day plan Iran conveyed through Qatar - a ceasefire extending to Lebanon, lifting of the naval blockade, oil-sanctions relief and release of frozen assets in exchange for reopening the strait on day six and nuclear talks on day seven - was refused, with the administration retaining the blockade and privately expecting a renewed bombing campaign after the November midterms. Hormuz transit therefore stays heavily restricted after nearly seven months of conflict. This is a Sunday-reopen repricing question, not a present one, and it is framed conditionally throughout the forecast. Shared Finviz context was read and is both stale relative to the 90-minute bound and partial: its futures and calendar sections were unavailable, while breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections were present as explicitly latest-session, non-real-time data. It was given no material weight and was never treated as evidence of live structure. Confidence opens at 82 on verified index, futures, volatility, yield, energy and calendar evidence, then decays to 76 by the final slot as the Friday reference ages beyond thirty-six hours without a refreshing tick. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a danger window inside a closed tape would be meaningless; next week's checkpoints - August PCE, final Q2 GDP and Chicago PMI on Wednesday, ISM manufacturing and jobless claims on Thursday, and September payrolls on Friday - all fall outside this window and are carried as conditional drivers.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 published hours the Claude state ranged between Tail 8 and 22 and never reached the block threshold. The September 25 European and US cash stretch from 10:00Z to 14:00Z produced trend-up and mixed prints at Tail 20-22 in WATCH as the index worked higher; the 13:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed. From 15:00Z the state returned to EA_ON at Tail 18-19 in a mixed mode, and after the 21:00Z futures settle it stepped down through Tail 12 to a stable 8-10 on a normal mode for the whole overnight closure. Stress fell from the mid-50s to the mid-40s over the same stretch while Confidence held between 82 and 88.
outlookSummary: The entire published window falls inside the scheduled weekend closure: futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, thirteen hours past the final slot. Tail is held between 7 and 8 for all 24 hours because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, and none of the inherited amplifiers - shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, or the index holding near an extreme - can be observed while every venue is shut. Every hour therefore maps to EA_ON and green. Stress eases from 47 toward 44 through the Saturday afternoon and evening as Friday's two-sided evidence ages without contradiction, then rebuilds to 48 into Sunday morning as the window tilts conditionally toward an unresolved reopen backdrop of post-crisis long-end yields, an elevated crude complex and a restricted Hormuz corridor after the reported refusal of Iran's seven-day plan. Confidence declines from 82 to 76 purely with evidence age. No danger window is published, and the reopening auction itself falls outside this window.
